evals.prompt: I'm starting a new Python data analysis project and want Claude Code available in a devcontainer so I can use AI assistance while working. Generate the devcontainer config for me — I need pandas, openpyxl, and httpx available, and I want Claude Code wired up so it's ready to use when the container starts.
evals.expected_output: A complete .devcontainer/devcontainer.json and .devcontainer/postCreate.sh that include the claude-code devcontainer feature, a named volume for persisting .claude config, Python feature with the requested packages pinned, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY passthrough. Should explain key decisions like the volume and key wiring.

assertions.description: devcontainer.json includes the Anthropic claude-code devcontainer feature URI
devcontainer.json includes the Python devcontainer feature
devcontainer.json mounts /home/vscode/.claude (or equivalent) as a named Docker volume
devcontainer.json wires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via remoteEnv or containerEnv, OR the response explicitly states OAuth was chosen as the auth method and explains why
postCreate.sh contains chown to fix ownership of the .claude volume directory
postCreate.sh installs pandas, openpyxl, and httpx

evals.prompt: I already have a working Claude devcontainer for my project. It has Python set up. Now I need to add Go to it so I can work on a Go service in the same environment. What changes do I need to make to devcontainer.json and postCreate.sh, and do I need to rebuild?
evals.expected_output: Specific diff showing the Go devcontainer feature to add to devcontainer.json, clear explanation that a rebuild is required, and any postCreate.sh changes needed. Should not regenerate the entire config from scratch — just the delta.

assertions.description: response includes the correct ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/go feature URI
response explicitly tells user that a container rebuild is required
response gives a focused change (not a full regenerated config) — shows only what to add

evals.prompt: I'm not using VS Code devcontainers — my team uses Docker Compose for our dev environment. I want to get Claude Code working in our setup so team members can use it inside the container. How do I do this? We're on Ubuntu 22.04.
evals.expected_output: Practical Docker Compose / Dockerfile approach for installing Claude Code (npm install -g or the devcontainer feature install script), how to mount a volume for .claude persistence, and how to pass ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via docker-compose environment. Should acknowledge this is outside the devcontainer feature ecosystem.

assertions.description: response shows a Docker named volume mount for .claude config persistence
response shows ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in a docker-compose environment section

evals.prompt: I'm setting up a devcontainer for a project that multiple teammates will clone and use. We share an API key via a team password manager. Set up a Claude-enabled devcontainer with Node.js — make sure the API key gets wired in so everyone can use Claude without having to log in via browser.
evals.expected_output: A complete devcontainer.json and postCreate.sh with the claude-code feature, Node.js feature, named volume for .claude, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY passed via remoteEnv. Should NOT rely on OAuth for this scenario. Should explain where teammates need to set the env var on their host.

assertions.description: devcontainer.json includes the Anthropic claude-code devcontainer feature URI
devcontainer.json includes a Node.js devcontainer feature
devcontainer.json mounts /home/vscode/.claude (or equivalent) as a named Docker volume
devcontainer.json wires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via remoteEnv or containerEnv — OAuth must NOT be the recommended auth method for this shared-team scenario
postCreate.sh contains chown to fix ownership of the .claude volume directory
